headline: Track & Field Competes in CTC Indoor Championships
transcription:
By Lou Villanueva

This past Friday, the Stevens track team continued its preparations for outdoor season by competing in the CTC Indoor Championships. In total the team set seventeen school records. Key finishes came in the Distance Medley Relay. A group of four freshman, Greg Smith, Ed Palange, Lance Nanek, and Rob Anderson, finished the race in second place with a time of (12:41:39).

Patrick Bastien posted a third place finish in the 500 meters (1:09.51) and sixth in the 200 meters (23.52). Top placing on the women's side was by Monica Johnson in the weight throw (28", 11.75")
summary: Stevens' track team set seventeen school records at the CTC Indoor Championships, with an all-freshman distance medley relay taking second place and Patrick Bastien placing third in the 500 meters.
notability_note: Team reportedly set seventeen school records at a single meet.
confidence_notes: The clipping is cropped at the bottom, so the article may continue beyond what is shown. The DMR time is printed as '(12:41:39)', which is an unusual format for a relay time and may be a typesetting error in the original. The weight throw mark '(28", 11.75")' is printed as shown and its meaning is unclear.

headline: Track Competes in MAC Championships
transcription:
By Lou Villanueva

The track team at Stevens Institute of Technology spent the weekend competing in the MAC Championships in New York, New York. Of the members of the team competing, a total of two school and four freshman records were set.

Finishing highest for Stevens was Sunny Kennedy, who took seventh place in the long jump (11'11"). For the men, the 4x200 relay team finished the highest. The team consists of Ed Palange, Andrew Molloy, Wayne Fontaine, and Rob Anderson. The team competes again on March 18 in the Stevens Invitational.
summary: Stevens competed at the MAC Championships in New York City, setting two school records and four freshman records; Sunny Kennedy's seventh in the long jump was the team's highest finish.
notability_note: Two school records and four freshman records set at the meet.

headline: Track Competes At Montclair
transcription:
By Lou Villanueva

The men's and women's track teams compete this Saturday at Montclair State University in the Montclair Invitational. Competition begins at 10:30 a.m. The team for the 2000 spring season consists of a number of talented young members. Coach Al Alonso stated, "We are lacking in experience, but have some people who have the potential to be very, very good," said Alonso. "I expect us to get progressively better as the season goes along."

Returning this year includes Patrick Bastien, who set two individual school records last year, along with running on a total of three relay teams. Focusing on short sprints will be Fred Mansell, Ed Palange, and junior Kevin Frei. On middle distance events, Tom Zapata, Greg Quinn, Robert Anderson, and Ted Vallejos will be taking charge. Longer distance events will be taken care of by the likes of Sachi Desai and Lance Nanek.

On hurdles and field Events, Coach Alonso hopes to see good results from Andre Deliso, Wayne Fontaine, Dario Peynado, and Vincent Lampa. Alonso stated, "Both Dario and Vincent have worked hard and had an immediate impact in their respective areas."

Leading up the women's team will be Anne Krone, Sunny Kennedy and Monica Johnson. "Anne has really improved this year and is setting a good example for our younger team members with her work ethic," praised Alonso. "Monica and Sunny have already broken records and have just scratched the surface on what should be two outstanding careers."

Working on distance events will be Yelena Havryliuk and Rachel Luch. Kennedy, Kameelah Majied, Naomi Chin, and Varuna Sundaram will be working on sprints. Chin and Kennedy will handle jumps as well. "Our women's team is short on depth, but we have several athletes who are capable of excelling in more than one area," said Alonso. "It is important that everyone stay healthy ... We've got dedicated athletes who are committed to making a name for Stevens Track and Field. They are going to gain some very important experience this year and as our numbers increase, we should get better and better in the future."
summary: A season-preview article ahead of the Montclair Invitational, in which coach Al Alonso runs through the young 2000 spring roster event group by event group and assesses the team's prospects.
notability_note: Detailed roster listing for the 2000 spring season with coach's assessment of each event group; useful as a record of team composition.
confidence_notes: The coach is named 'Al Alonso' here but appears as 'Adalberto Alonso' in later cross country articles — presumably the same person. Some names (Havryliuk, Kameelah Majied, Varuna Sundaram) are printed on a slightly faded scan; readings appear correct but are lower confidence than the rest.

headline: Track Competes In Montclair State University Invitational
transcription:
By Lou Villanueva

This past Saturday, the Stevens Men's and Women's Track and Field Team competed in the Montclair Invitational. Earlier, the Ducks hosted the Stevens Invitational on March 18. At the Invitational, the women's team took a second place overall finish. The men finished the day coming out in fifth place overall.

During the Montclair event, Monica Johnson set a school record in the discus- throwing event. She threw for a total of 96' 2". This gave her a second place finish in the event. She also set a school record in the javelin throw as well. Johnson threw for a total of 101' 8". Placing fourth place in the hammer throw was Vincent Lampa, with Johnson taking fifth place. Placing fifth in the 3000 meter Steeple Chase was Lance Nanek, who finished in a time of 12:41.9. The team's next meet is on Saturday April 1, in Wayne for the Pioneer Relays at 9 a.m.
summary: At the Montclair Invitational, Monica Johnson set Stevens school records in both the discus (96'2") and the javelin (101'8"); the article also recaps the team's second (women) and fifth (men) place finishes at the Stevens Invitational on March 18.
notability_note: Monica Johnson set two school records (discus and javelin) at the same meet.

headline: Track and Field Places
transcription:
By Elena Ziarnik

This past weekend Stevens track and field made a good showing at the St. John's invitational in Jamaica, NY. The team's freshmen took the top places in the competition.

Freshmen Monica Johnson and Rachel Luch placed fourth throwing 9.61 meters and tenth throwing 4.92 meters in the shot putt respectively. For the men's team, freshmen Vincent Lampa placed fifth in shot putt throwing 9.84 meters. Freshmen Lance Nanek and Greg Smith placed seventh and eighth respectively in the 3000 meter steeplechase as well.

The two teams compete again April 15 at the CTC Championships in New York.
summary: Stevens freshmen led the team at the St. John's Invitational, with Monica Johnson fourth and Vincent Lampa fifth in the shot put and Lance Nanek and Greg Smith seventh and eighth in the steeplechase.
confidence_notes: 'shot putt' spelling is as printed in the original.

headline: Track Competes At Bergen Relays
transcription:
By Lou Villanueva

The men's and women's track and field teams competed in the Bergen CC Relay Carnival last Saturday. Both teams saw players from each compete individually.

On the women's side, Sunny Kennedy ended up placing fourth in the shot putt relay and second place in the javelin relay. Kennedy ended up having a combined throw of 15.81 in the shot put and 47.86 m in the javelin. She also placed fourth in the long jump and set another record in the 100-meter hurdle. Overall, the team placed second out of a total of nine teams.

[...]

For the men, Vince Lampa along with Greg Quinn took a fifth place finish in the shot putt relay. Lampa also teamed with Lance Nanek to take a fifth place finish in the javelin relay. Placing second in the distance medley-relay was Quinn again with a time of 12:05.94. The team ended up finishing in fifth place out of a total of eleven schools total.
summary: At the Bergen CC Relay Carnival the Stevens women placed second of nine teams, led by Sunny Kennedy, who set another record in the 100-meter hurdles; the men finished fifth of eleven.
notability_note: Sunny Kennedy set a record in the 100-meter hurdles (the article does not specify school or freshman record).
confidence_notes: The clipping is split into two fragments with material apparently missing between the women's and men's sections, so the transcription may not be continuous. Kennedy's shot put mark '15.81' is printed without a unit.

headline: Cross Country Opens Up At William Paterson
transcription:
By Lou Villanueva

The Men's and Women's Cross Country teams started up their 2000 fall seasons competing in the William Paterson Invitational at Garrett Mountain. Coach Adalberto Alonso saw this first competition as more of a "learner" course for all the new faces to the team.

"We used this first race to simply get some experience for some of our younger runners," said Alonso. "I expect some major improvement this weekend when we compete at Wagner."

On the women's side, Rebecca Dougherty finished first for Stevens with a time of 22:14. Melissa McAvoy finished second for the team with a time of 25:35. Rounding out third was Louise Firmer in 26:37. The women's team had an 11th place overall finish.

For the men, Nick Dunford was first for the Ducks, taking a seventh place finish with a time of 30:29. Second for Stevens was Colin McKinley in 30:55 and third was Sachi Desai in 30:55. They placed nineteenth and twentieth overall, respectively.

"This was a good start for us, considering we didn't run some of our stronger runners," said Coach Alonso. "It's good to get off to a strong start, and this season appears to be very promising."
summary: Stevens opened the 2000 cross country season at the William Paterson Invitational, with Rebecca Dougherty leading the women (22:14, 11th as a team) and Nick Dunford leading the men with a seventh-place finish.
confidence_notes: McKinley and Desai are both given the identical time of 30:55 while being placed nineteenth and twentieth — printed as shown, possibly a typo in the original. Dunford's surname is spelled 'Dunford' here and 'Dunnford' in the following week's article.

headline: X-Country Takes Fourth
transcription:
By Lou Villanueva

Men's cross-country competed with the women this past weekend at the Wagner Invitational. Out of a total of eleven Division III teams, Stevens placed fourth overall.

Leading the team was the strong finishing times of newcomers Colin McKinley and Nick Dunnford. McKinley finished twenty-eighth overall with a (30:14) time, with Dunnford finishing just after at (30:18). Coach Alonso commented on both of their efforts stating, "I think the two of them will push each other and their personal rivalry will help bring out the best in each of their performances."

Improving by a total of three minutes over last week's performance was Stevens O'Neill with a time of (31:37) and a 53 place finish. "Steve has made a dramatic improvement in only one week of cross country racing," Alonso stated. "Before last week he had not been running. I look forward to [See X-COUNTRY, Page 10]

[From X-COUNTRY, Page 12] a very promising season from him as he continues to improve.

Rounding out the top five finishers were Sachi Desai (31:37), and Ted Vallejos (32:19).

Coach Alonso's overall impression of his team so far is a positive one. "Right now our overall team average is over a minute faster that last year. I've said it before and I'll say it again ... this team has the potential to be one of the best in school history. Of course that statement is contingent upon us working hard, getting better, and staying healthy."
summary: The Stevens men placed fourth of eleven Division III teams at the Wagner Invitational behind freshmen Colin McKinley and Nick Dunnford, with coach Alonso noting the team average was more than a minute faster than the previous year.
confidence_notes: 'Stevens O'Neill' is printed as such but is almost certainly Steve O'Neill, as the following sentence refers to 'Steve'. The jump line reads 'See X-COUNTRY, Page 10' while the continuation reads 'From X-COUNTRY, Page 12' — inconsistency is in the original. O'Neill and Desai are both credited with (31:37); printed as shown.

headline: Women Place At WIAC Championships
transcription:
By Lou Villanueva

The women's cross country, along with finishing well at the Wagner College Inviitaional this weekend, finished out the week by placing second in the WIAC Championships on Sunday. Overall in the meet the team palces seventh out of ten division III teams competing.

"The WIAC Championship came down to a very close race between us and Ramapo, said Coach Alonso, "It was a tough overall battle against a team that featured some veterans and a new runner we had not seen before."

Leading the team was Rebecca Dougherty, who came in overall with a time of (22:43). Melissa McAvoy finished up in sixth with a time of (23:41). "Both Rebecca and Melissa are coming along nicely," continued coach Alonso, "They're both working extremely hard each day and i expect them to continue to get better each week as the season progresses."

The Ducks individual times were all suprisingly decent, considering the inexperience of some of the team. Newcomer Megan Rzepski ran a (24:28) in her first competition ever. "Megan ran a very respectable time considering it was her very first race.", said Alonso, "Like the rest of our team Megan will continue to improve as she gains experience. Included in the top six finishers for the Lady Ducks were Maureen Amador (23:41), Louise Firmer (24:08) and Tiia Piller (28:14) Stevens continues its season with a dual meet against CCNY this Sunday at Van Cordlandt Park."
summary: The Stevens women followed the Wagner College Invitational with a championship meet in which they narrowly lost out to Ramapo, led by Rebecca Dougherty (22:43) and Melissa McAvoy (23:41); newcomer Megan Rzepski ran her first-ever race.
notability_note: Conference/championship meet coverage; also records Megan Rzepski's first competitive race.
confidence_notes: The article contradicts itself, saying the team placed second in the championship and also that it 'palces seventh out of ten' — both printed as shown. Misspellings ('Inviitaional', 'palces', 'suprisingly', 'Van Cordlandt') are in the original. 'WIAC' as printed is unusual for an East Coast meet and may be a typo for another conference acronym; the meet is not identified elsewhere in the deck. The closing quotation marks around Alonso's final quote are placed inconsistently in the original, so it is unclear where his quote ends and the reporter's text resumes.

headline: Cross Country Races at Drew
transcription:
By Lou Villanueva

Both men's and women's cross country teams competed this past weekend at the Drew Invitational. On the Lady Ducks' side, the team finished in third place. The men took a fourth place finish in their division.

Taking the lead for the women was Rebecaa Dougherty with a 12 place finish in a time of (23:12). Up next in line for Stevens was Maureen Amador. Amador finished up 13 with a time of (23:45). In third for Stevens was Melissa Mcavoy in a time of (25:00). Rounding out the top five finishers for the school was Louise Firmer (25:04) and Megan Rzepski (25:09).

On the men's team, finishing first for the Ducks was Colin McKinlet, with Nick Dunford close behind. Both members finished in (29:19) and (29:23), respectively. In third was Sachi Desai in (29:34), with Steve O'Neill (31:19) and Shafik Quoraishee (31:56) topping out the top 5. Both the teams compete again at the Stevens Invitational this Saturday.
summary: Stevens' women placed third and the men fourth at the Drew Invitational, with Rebecca Dougherty and Colin McKinley leading their respective squads.

headline: Cross Country Takes 2nd At Stevens Invitational
transcription:
By Lou Villanueva

Both men's and women's cross country teams competed at the Stevens Invitational at Liberty State Park this past weekend. The Ducks had a good turnout on both the male and female side as both teams went on to take a second place overall finish is the invitational. The finish saw the women place higher than rival Drew and then the men did better than tough competitor Army Prep.

For the Lady Ducks, Rebecca Dougherty finished first for the team with an eleventh place time of 22:41. Coming in second was Louise Firner in fourteenth with a 23:05 finish, and in third and fourth were Maureen Amador and Megan Rzepski with times of 23:05 and 23:28 respectively. "I was very pleased with the performance of our women this weekend," said head coach Adalberto Alonso. "We're continuing to make steady progress and the results are starting to show."

Coach Alonso also had good words for this men's team as well, in regards to their second place finish. "I thought all of our runners ran a very smart race," Alonso said. "Saturday's performance shows that we're continuing to progress and mature as a team." First for the team was Sachi Desai taking a third place overall finish in 28:06. In second for Stevens was Nick Dunford, followed closely behind yet again by Colin Mckinley. They both finished 7th and 9th respectively in times of 28:34 and 28:38. Rounding out the top six were Steve O'Neill (29:43), Gabe Miani (30:35) and Ted Vallejos (3[?]:35)
summary: Both Stevens squads took second overall at their home Stevens Invitational at Liberty State Park, the women beating rival Drew and the men beating Army Prep; Sachi Desai was third overall for the men.
confidence_notes: Ted Vallejos's time is degraded in the scan — the minutes digit after '3' is illegible, so it reads roughly '3?:35'; it may duplicate Miani's 30:35. 'Louise Firner' is printed as such but is Louise Firmer elsewhere in the deck. Firner and Amador are both credited with 23:05 while placed second and third; printed as shown.

headline: Cross Country Team Competes In Skyline Championships
meet_or_event: Skyline Conference Championships (Sunken Meadow State Park)
transcription:
By Lou Villanueva

The men's and women's cross country teams competed in their first ever Skyline Conference Championships this past weekend. Both teams finished in second place overall. The Championships took place at Sunken Meadow State Park in Long Island.

For the women, Coach Al Alonso thought the team did well, while losing to first place finisher St Joe's Patchogue. "Everyone ran well for us, but it was a tough loss to one of our rivals in St. Joseph's-Patchogue," said head coach Al Alonso. "This weekend we have another shot at them in our Halloween Classic and we're looking forward to the opportunity to avenge our defeat."

Finishing fifth and sixth place overall were Rebecca Dougherty and Maureen Amador, in times of (23:43) and (25:09), respectively. Rounding out the top five for Stevens were Louise Firmer (26:21), Anne Krone (26:37), and Megan Rzepski (26:41).

"It was a very strange meet because we got caught in the back of the pack at the start," Alonso said. "I'm very proud of the fact that our team kept moving into contention and continued to pick people off as the race progressed."

On the men's side, The Ducks also finished second place overall. Taking first place for Stevens and third place overall was Gabe Miani in a time of (29:31). Taking a fourth place overall finish and second for the Ducks was Sachi Desai in a time of (29:45). "Gabe ran a very good race, and it's amazing to me that he's progressed as quickly as he has," stated Alonso. "Right now he's just about running at the level that I expect him to."

summary: In Stevens' first Skyline Conference Championships, both teams finished second overall, the women losing out to St. Joseph's-Patchogue and the men led by Gabe Miani's third-place overall finish.

headline: Cross Country Places Well At Halloween Classic
meet_or_event: Stevens Halloween Collegiate Classic (Van Cortlandt Park)
transcription:
By Lou Villanueva

The men's and women's cross country teams competed at Van Cortlandt Park this past Sunday in the Stevens Halloween Collegiate Classic. Both teams end up producing their best average times at the park in the Bronx ever. Both teams also finished the day in second place overall.

For the men, placing first was Sachi Desai, whose time of 28:51 was good enough to get him a sixth place overall individual finish. Finishing 7 overall and second of Stevens was Gabriel Miani in a time of 28:51. Rounding out the top three for the men was Nick Dunford in an 8 place overall finish of 29:13.

On the women's side, Rebecca Dougherty led the pack of Ducks with a time of 22:12, placing 12 overall. In second for the women was Maureen Amador, with a 14 overall finish time of 22:36. In third was Megan Rzepski, taking 21 place with a time of 23:25.

Both the men's and the women's teams travel to Tufts University this Saturday to take part in the ECAC Championships.
summary: Both Stevens teams finished second overall at their own Halloween Collegiate Classic at Van Cortlandt Park and posted their best-ever average times on that course.
notability_note: Both teams reportedly produced their best-ever average times at Van Cortlandt Park.
confidence_notes: Desai and Miani are both credited with 28:51 while placed sixth and seventh overall; printed as shown.

headline: Men's And Women's Cross Country Finish Season
transcription:
The men's and the women's cross country teams both finished up their seasons this past Saturday, with a competition at the NCAA Atlantic Regionals. Held at the University of Rochester, the Ducks took twenty sixth place finishes in both the men's and the women's divisions.

A swarm of personal bests were completed this past weekend, with Rebecca Dougherty finishing first for the Ducks. She got a personal best time of (21:23).

"Rebecca ended the season by running an outstanding time under very difficult circumstances," head coach Al Alonso said. "The course was very muddy and slippery, and Rebecca's performance is a tribute to her hard work and concentration."

Taking second for Stevens was senior Captain Anne Krone in a personal record time of (23:49).

"Anne's loss is going to be a big one for our team," Alonso said. "We're certainly going to miss her leadership and enthusiasm because she was the key to our season. Anne helped us go from a rebuilding year to one of the best seasons in school history. Rounding out the top three for the Ducks was Tiia Piller in 175 place, with a personal best time of (26:00).

For the men, Sachi Desai and Nick Dunford took the 115 and 120 places, respectively, with times of (27:43) and (27:48).

"Sachi and Nick both went into the regionals with the goal of running under (28:00), and that's exactly what they did," Alonso stated. "It was nice to see them perform up to their expectations in the biggest race of the year."

In 157 place was Colin McKinley, with a personal best time of (28:44).

"I was proud of Colin because we were looking for him to break 29:00," Alonso said. "He wrapped up a fine freshman year with his personal best time."

In spite of the fact that he fell early in the race, Shafik Quorashiee still managed to break the thirty-minute mark and finish the race in (28:44).

summary: Stevens closed the 2000 season at the NCAA Atlantic Regionals in Rochester, both teams taking twenty-sixth, with personal bests from Rebecca Dougherty (21:23), senior captain Anne Krone (23:49), Tiia Piller, Colin McKinley and others on a muddy course.
